name: TinyOS_enhanced
description: Fully upgraded, security-focused version of the TinyOS hobby OS

paragraphs: A from-scratch, security-focused 32-bit (i386) operating system kernel, written in C and x86 assembly. Boots via Multiboot2/GRUB, runs in QEMU, and demonstrates a full vertical slice of OS concepts — protected mode, PAE paging with NX/W^X, preemptive multitasking, ring-3 user processes, a TCP/IP stack on a real NIC driver, from-scratch cryptography, and ECDSA-signed-ELF secure boot enforced by default.
Successor to douglasmun/TinyOS — substantially expanded in scope, security, and reliability.

whatItDoes.text: A from-scratch, security-focused 32-bit (i386) operating system kernel, written in C and x86 assembly. Boots via Multiboot2/GRUB, runs in QEMU, and demonstrates a full vertical slice of OS concepts — protected mode, PAE paging with NX/W^X, preemptive multitasking, ring-3 user processes, a TCP/IP stack on a real NIC driver, from-scratch cryptography, and ECDSA-signed-ELF secure boot enforced by default.

requirements.text: Boot → shell → login — Multiboot2 boot, first-boot root password setup, PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 (100k iterations) password hashing.

Ring-3 login shell — login lands in an unprivileged ring-3 shell (35 builtins) that reaches the kernel only through syscalls; password prompts happen in the kernel, so the shell never holds a password. kshell hands over to the kernel shell for networking and security tooling.
